The final portfolio must contain at least five well-supported stories in every category. Treat social attention as a discovery signal rather than verification. More than half of the final stories must originate with independent, local or social discovery, using the first source in each story as the discovery source; established outlets may account for no more than half.

items.title: J&K High Court stays CAT Jammu order imposing ₹10,000 costs on senior advocate
items.summary: The High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh has stayed the operation of an order passed by the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT), Jammu Bench, imposing costs of ₹10,000 on Senior Advocate Jahangir Ganai. A Division Bench of Justices Sanjeev Kumar and MA Chowdhary passed the interim order while hearing the senior advocate’s writ petition against the Tribunal’s order. Justice Sanjeev Kumar and Justice M A Choudhary The CAT had imposed the costs after recording that Ganai appeared before it during virtual proceedings without wearing uniform and made derogatory remarks against it. The Tribunal had also observed that he appeared to be unapologetic about appearing without uniform. After hearing counsel for the parties, the High Court observed that “the case for indulgence at this stage is made out.” The Division Bench expressed its intention to mediate and explore an amicable settlement. The Court directed the tribunal members concerned and the petitioners to appear in person before it in chambers on October 21. “In the meanwhile, there shall be stay of the effect and operation of the impugned order,” the High Court directed. items.title: Gauhati High Court grants bail to accused in Zubeen Garg murder case
items.summary: The Gauhati High Court recently granted bail to Amritprava Mahanta, an accused in the alleged murder of Assamese singer Zubeen Garg, after finding that the investigation materials and evidence recorded during trial did not disclose a prima facie case against her [Amritprava Mahanta v. State of Assam]. Justice Pranjal Das observed that continuing Mahanta's detention despite the absence of supporting evidence would amount to a travesty of justice. " Considering the nature of the materials found on record so far, with regard to A-4 Amritprava Mahanta, it would be a travesty of justice to deny her bail at this stage, especially when she has already undergone undertrial detention for almost a year now, " the Court said. Justice Pranjal Das Garg died in Singapore on September 19, 2025, after an incident during a yacht trip. Following complaints alleging murder, the Assam Police's Criminal Investigation Department registered a case and eventually chargesheeted seven persons. items.title: Can courts accept written statements beyond 120-day deadline? Delhi High Court larger bench to decide
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently referred to a larger bench the question of whether courts can permit defendants in civil suits to file their written statements beyond the prescribed 120-day deadline. [Yogesh Taneja v. Vinay Taneja] A Division Bench of Justices Vivek Chaudhary and Renu Bhatnagar expressed disagreement with earlier decisions of coordinate benches holding that the 120-day deadline under the Delhi High Court (Original Side) Rules, 2018 is mandatory and cannot be extended. The Court was of the prima facie view that the provision is procedural in nature and should be interpreted in accordance with Supreme Court judgments permitting extensions in exceptional circumstances. The Bench observed that the language of the Delhi High Court Rules was substantially similar to the corresponding provision of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC), which the Supreme Court had interpreted as directory rather than mandatory. "Thus, applying the same principle, the only possible interpretation is that Rule 4 of DHC Rules is also directory in nature, leaving the same discretion with the High Court, as is available to any other Courts to which Order VIII Rule 1 CPC applies, " the Court said. items.title: Plea in Supreme Court seeks contempt action against Congress party for post against CJI
items.summary: A petition filed before the Supreme Court has sought guidelines to bar political parties from running public campaigns that target a judge or the Chief Justice of India (CJI) in relation to pending matters, outside the procedure for removal of judges laid down in the Constitution. The plea has been filed following a post by the X handle of the Kerala unit of the Congress on October 12, which said, "Dear Surya Kant, If law and order is not your domain, resign now. We will find your replacement who can handle it." The petition says the post addressed the CJI by name, without the courtesy of his title and sought to coerce a sitting Chief Justice who had declined to discuss sub-judice matters outside the courtroom. It also refers to a post by Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra the same evening, "Surya clearly Can't. So we will." Besides the Union government, the Congress Party, Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee, Mahua Moitra and Akhilesh Yadav have been made respondents to the plea. items.title: Supreme Court asks Delhi government to seek IB inputs on jail transfer plea by CM Beant Singh assassination convict
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday asked the Delhi government to obtain inputs from the Intelligence Bureau (IB) on whether Jagtar Singh Hawara, who is serving a life sentence for his role in the 1995 assassination of former Punjab Chief Minister Beant Singh, can be transferred from Tihar Jail to a prison in Punjab [ Jagtar Singh Hawara v. Govt. of NCT of Delhi ]. A Bench of Justices MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale issued the direction while considering Hawara's plea for the jail transfer. Additional Solicitor General (ASG) Aishwarya Bhati , appearing for the Delhi government, told the Court that IB inputs were necessary before a decision could be taken in the matter. Bhati submitted that transfers should be avoided if the Intelligence Bureau provided adverse inputs. She added that the Punjab government had filed an affidavit stating that the transfer should not be considered in the interest of maintaining peace and tranquillity. items.title: Kerala High Court deletes its adverse remarks against advocate over false affidavit attestation
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Tuesday expunged adverse remarks made by a single judge Bench of the Court against a young lawyer for allegedly allowing his client to file an affidavit containing false statements in a bank account freeze case. A Division Bench of Justice Devan Ramachandran and Justice Basant Balaji observed that although the adverse remarks were meant to caution young lawyers about their professional duties, such remarks could permanently affect the lawyer's legal career. The Court, therefore, agreed to remove such comments from the record. " No doubt, of course, the judgement speaks with a slightly harsh stone, but we are of the view that it was not intended to be so, but only to caution the counsel so that he will be more careful in the future. With that said, it will not be proper for us to leave the portions of that judgement, which appear to speak against the council without being interfered with, for the singular reason that this will certainly have an impact on his future perpetually, " the Court said. Justice Suraj Govindaraj also made strong observations on the seriousness of the allegations, while dismissing petitions filed by the accused seeking to quash the case against them. “These (allegations) are (more) serious than IPC 302 (murder),” the Court observed. The Court noted that this affected her reputation, particularly since the content was shared in the locality where she worked. The woman worked as an assistant professor at a private college in Puttur. Unknown persons allegedly circulated an obscene video in a WhatsApp group, along with details of her Instagram handle and her photograph. items.title: Misbehaviour with lawyer discharging duty is contempt of court: Allahabad High Court
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court on Monday observed that any misbehavior with lawyer in connection with court proceedings will amount to contempt of court as they are officers of the Court [Sachin Yadav v State of UP] Justice Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal made the observation while dealing with a case in which the PRO of a Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) was accused of misbehaving with a government counsel over phone. "Whenever they [government counsel] inform to any officer about the compliance of the order of this Court, they are discharging their duty in compliance of the order of the Court and misbehaving with them by any officer may be the top-most officer of the State will amount to contempt," the Court said. Considering that PRO Rajesh Kumar Singh had misbehaved with Additional Government Advocate Anurag Pandey when he was trying to inform him about court's orders in a bail matter, the bench ordered that Singh be kept in the Court's custody till 5 PM. "This Court instead of passing any stricture against him, directs that he be taken into custody and he will remain in the custody of court till 5 pm, whereafter he shall be released," it said. items.title: First come first serve policy to allot grounds for Ramleela unfair: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has directed Delhi government authorities to frame comprehensive guidelines every year for allotment of public grounds for Ramleela and similar cultural or religious events [Ray of New Beginning Foundation v. Delhi Urban Shelter Improvement Board & Ors] . Justice Amit Mahajan passed the order on October 8, holding that a “first come, first serve” policy for allotment of such spaces is constitutionally unreasonable and can create unequal opportunities for applicants. The Court reasoned that at first sight, the expression “first come first serve” seems to embody an objective rule, but it creates an unequal race for information by incentivising the discovery of availability of a public ground before competing applicants become aware of it. “The same creates a structural dilemma, that is, a person with privileged access to administrative information may obtain an advantage that is unavailable to others,” the Court said. Justice Amit Mahajan, Delhi High Court Therefore, it directed the authorities to publish annual site-allocation notices at least 90 days before the first scheduled event.
